newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania president concedes defeat of his party.
newsitem.headline: Albania president concedes defeat of his party.

text.p: President Sali Berisha on Monday conceded his Democratic Party has lost Albania's general election and urged supporters to work hard in opposition to a new government energing after a left-wing victory.
But Berisha failed to make clear in a television address whether he intended to stay in office as allowed by post-communist legislation.

"Albanian voters yesterday seemingly voted that the Democratic Party should be in opposition. On this occasion I would like to express my deepest gratitude to those hundreds and thousands of Albanians...who supported the Democratic Party," Berisha said.

"I invite all these electors, all the members, activists, sympathisers of the Democratic Party to treat yesterday's verdict with courage and dignity and to continue together ...our efforts as an opposition to consolidate democracy."
Berisha, speaking calmly, told viewers the will of voters would be respected. "I will also fully respect unflichingly all my previous statements," he said.
Berisha said before and during the election campaign that he would quit if a leftist government came to power, but his statement left unclear what course he intended to take.

Socialist leader Fatos Nano, who claimed a sweeping victory on Sunday evening after the polls closed, said Berisha had lost his last chance to remain in office alongside any administration headed by left-wing parties.

"Berisha lost his final chance for 'cohabitation' with the Albanian people and the political forces that represent them," Nano told a news conference before Berisha's admission of defeat was known. "All Albanians expect Berisha to resign."

Berisha, first elected by parliament in 1992, must submit any resignation to the country's newly-elected assembly. He was re-elected by the assembly to a new four-year term on March 3, one day after deputies proclaimed a state of emergency to quell an upsurge of violence in the country,
Berisha made no mention of the Socialists in his address. The Socialists say they have won around 60 of the 115 seats being contested.
